entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

I spelled out what it means: version 1, every migration path removed (not just the new 3→4 step), and any file with a different version loads as a fresh, empty document. That last part means project-state files you saved during development will lose their chats. I also told it not to start the live batch until you approve one. Its native build finished cleanly at 17:23. Its tests haven't run yet.

## Plan for the live batch

**First, at no cost.** Run the native and shell-harness tests, then re-record `tests/project_prompt/requests.json` with the scripted model. Those recordings still contain the removed `origin` field.

**Batch A: the standard project-prompt evaluation. 75 runs.**
- All 25 cases, 3 runs each, on DeepSeek V4 Flash with the pinned host. I run only the new prompt and compare it case by case with the October 19 baseline, as you asked earlier today.
- Why it's needed: the change alters three things the model reads in every conversation. The `plan_set` description is new, the `origin` field is gone, and the plan now stays "current" after the agent's own edits.
- Cost: the October 19 baseline used about 1.2M input tokens for the same 75 runs, about 0.9M of them cached. I expect about the same.

**Batch B: headline journeys in the real app. 12 runs.**
- 4 cases, 3 runs each: a strength print, an appearance print that needs supports, a quick fit-check prototype, and a changed strategy. In the last one, a second message changes the goal and the headline should change with it.
- Each run loads one model into a clean project and lets the live agent work with real tools. This is not the canned-reply setup that wasted tokens on October 10. The harness's limit is 40 tool calls per turn; I'd lower it to 20.
- For every run I'd report:
  - the exact headline and its word count;
  - whether the agent called `plan_set` at all;
  - in the changed-strategy case, whether the headline was rewritten or stayed stale;
  - what the card showed at the end.
- No pass/fail thresholds: I read each run and tell you what looks wrong. Three runs per case won't give a reliable rate. They will show whether headlines are usually missing or generic, which was the October 12 problem.
- Cost is a guess, because no real-app journey has been measured: about 500k input tokens per run (roughly 20 requests at about 25k each, mostly cached), so about 6M for all 12.
- To limit that risk, I'd run one journey first, report its actual token use, and only run the other 11 if it's within twice the estimate. If it costs more, I come back to you.

**Total:** 87 runs, about 7M input tokens estimated. I'd log usage from every response and report the actual total.

entries.name: mcp__ccd_session__start_session
entries.description:
Start a separate Claude Code session for a task while you stay with the user (when: see "Starting other sessions"). `initiation` says who wants it: "user_asked" starts it now and returns its id; "offer" is for a task the user named in their latest message (new work here, or "suggest / split off / make a task or session for X"): called with a title alone, it shows a "New session" / "Do it here" card and WAITS for their answer, so it must be the only call in that message (no update_plan, no other tool); the result then tells you to carry on here, or to send the brief with proposal_id so the session starts; "own_initiative" is for work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up (when your reply calls work a follow-up or a separate PR, propose it here rather than only saying so); the user sees a card and nothing runs until they start it, by clicking it or by telling you (then call this again with just proposal_id).
"user_asked" and "own_initiative" both need a `prompt` — the brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like — and the call is refused without it; `background` does not stand in for it. Only an "offer" is a title alone.
context: "fork" = this whole conversation + your `prompt`. "fresh" (default) = your `prompt` + `background` only, so `background` is required too, at least 80 characters.
Checkout here ("fresh" only): use_worktree false = shares this checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session its branch and PR too: never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); true = its own worktree (the default when this session is in one).
Elsewhere ("fresh", user_asked only, when the user named the place): `cwd`, `target` "ssh" + `host`, `environment` or `preset`; list_start_targets lists the valid names.

initiation.description: "user_asked": the user asked in words for separate, parallel or background work, or told you to start this piece — it starts now. "offer": a task the user named in their latest message (new work for this session, or one they asked you to suggest, split off or make a session for) — the user is asked first and the call waits for their answer; send only title with it (the brief follows, with proposal_id, if they choose New session). "own_initiative": work you propose yourself that the user has not told you to do — something you noticed, or the follow-up your own answer or work turned up; it waits as a proposal card until the user starts it; never for a task the user's message tells you to do. Required unless proposal_id is set.

proposal_id.description: Start a proposal the user told you to start, exactly as proposed: its task_id and nothing else (wake_when_done may accompany a local one). To change it, dismiss_task it and start a new session.

title.description: Under 60 chars; names the task. Shown on the row or card. Required unless proposal_id is set.

prompt.description: The brief: the task, the files or area, what done looks like. Required for "user_asked" and "own_initiative" — the call is refused without it, and `background` does not stand in for it; an "offer" leaves it out (the card shows the user's own message) and you send it with proposal_id once they choose New session.

context.description: "fresh" (default) or "fork" — see the tool description. A "fork" from a worktree session gets a fresh worktree, normally cut from your branch tip (commit first; uncommitted edits stay here); from a plain checkout it shares the folder.

background.description: Required with "fresh", besides `prompt`: at least 80 characters of overall goal, decisions and constraints so far, how this piece fits — for someone who has not seen this conversation. Ignored for "fork".

wake_when_done.description: Once this session (and any sibling still working) ends its turn, or fails to start (unless it waits at a prompt the user answers there, its folder was never opened in Claude Desktop, or the user started, stopped or archived it), and you are idle, the app continues you, whether or not this is set. true also continues you if this session never gets its task some other way, such as a brief that is not sent; default false; not with own_initiative; ignored with target "cloud", which never continues you.

name.description: Optional short handle for the session ([a-z0-9-], ≤24), e.g. "cli-cleanup". Linked sessions and plan steps refer to it by this name; derived from the title when omitted.

use_worktree.description: "fresh" only (rejected with "fork"). false = shares this session's checkout and can edit it (in a worktree session: its worktree, branch and PR, so never for work that ends in a branch or PR of its own or belongs in another repository); not accepted from a session set up to move from the user's checkout into a worktree with EnterWorktree (before or after it moves), one working in a worktree on an SSH host, or one whose worktree was given back. At another place named by `cwd`, `host` or `preset`, false = that folder as it is. true = its own git worktree. content.text:
The setup-card headline work is committed as f964221268 on branch `claude/setup-card-headline` (not pushed), and the approved live batch is done. I checked the branch myself: the commit is there, the working tree is clean, the schema version is 1, and no migration code is left. The [implementation session](#local_cbad1a66-0d1c-4d7c-848b-8ec06545874b) reports that all tests pass (338 native agent-bridge cases, 444 page tests, and the shell-harness and real-adapter harness runs). I didn't rerun them.

**What changed:**
- The setup card shows the plan headline where the preset differences used to be.
- Each chat stores its own intent and plan. A new chat starts with no plan.
- The in-app agent's own edits no longer mark its plan as stale.
- The `origin` field and the code that tracked which settings the agent wrote are gone.
- "N objects with overrides" stays on its own line.
- The schema reset affects your files: project-state files saved during development will load as empty documents and lose their chats.

**The live batch: 12 journeys on DeepSeek V4 Flash, 4.5M input tokens (3.7M cached) and 91k output.**
- All 12 runs called `plan_set` and produced a headline of 7 to 12 words.
- In all three changed-strategy runs the headline was rewritten after the goal changed. For example, "Spiral vase mode for a lightweight, single-wall dried-flower vase" became "Multi-wall vase with infill for watertight strength, PLA on X1 Carbon."
- That's a clear improvement over October 12, when one journey never called `plan_set` and the other two were generic.

**What still looks wrong:**
- **Headlines still mention things the prompt says to leave out.** Five name the object ("PETG wall hook", "Rhino figurine"), one repeats the purpose ("for 5 kg load"), one names the printer, and one ends on routine preparation ("proper bed choice"). The extra words make headlines longer, but none is misleading.
- **The purpose title went stale in two changed-strategy runs.** The model rewrote the headline but never updated the purpose, so the card read "spiral vase for dried flowers" above a multi-wall watertight strategy. This prompt problem existed before this branch. I've proposed it as a separate follow-up (the card above).
- **A headline can arrive before its settings.** In one run, the new headline showed above the old spiral-vase estimates. The handoff accepted this, since a headline states intent, not applied settings.
- **Pictures were removed from every request.** The pinned model hosts reject images, so the model never saw the plate pictures. The batch says nothing about behavior that depends on them.

Not tested end to end: that the card's own Undo button counts as your edit. The code and a fake-workspace test say it does, but it wasn't exercised through the real button.

=== 28d6d67fdc
Merge intent_update and plan_set into one tool, setup_record

In batch B's changed-strategy runs the model rewrote the plan headline with
plan_set but never called intent_update, so the setup card's title still
named the old goal above the new strategy. The two records make up the card
and were already handled as one (same coordinator block, both in-app only,
both on the chat, the same context push), so they become one tool.

setup_record takes:
- setupTitle, required on every call: what the person wants, in their words.
  Restating it with each plan keeps title and headline from drifting apart.
  A title the chat refuses (more than one line or 120 characters) records
  nothing, the plan included.
- fields, optional, with intent_update's semantics (assumed, question,
  provenance).
- plan, optional: headline, decisions, assumptions, risks. Given, it
  replaces the whole plan; left out, the plan is kept. A purpose can be
  recorded before a strategy exists: a title-only call, the setup check,
  then a later call with the plan.
The result carries the intent section, purposeChange and the setup in force
as intent_update's did, and always the plan as it now stands. The
description keeps the concise-headline wording and states the split: the
title is what the person wants, the headline is how the agent will print.

The setup-changed skill fires on a setup_record whose purposeChange is
first or changed (a first purpose or changed fields), as before; a new
title alone is title_only, and a call that only restates the purpose to
change the plan is unchanged, so neither fires it. The card's context is
pushed once per successful call, so title and headline arrive together.

Changes to the model's input: one tool where there were two (27 project
tools, not 28), the project prompt's "recorded with setup_record", and the
setup-changed skill's "record the plan and its assumptions with
setup_record first". tests/project_prompt: grading, script, README,
project_tools.json and requests.json updated and re-recorded with the
scripted model; no live calls.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M5BMQDRNV2BHT3S97D58ZP7P

=== f964221268
Store intent and plan on each chat; show the plan headline on the setup card

Each chat now owns its print intent, purpose setup and plan. The project's
current ones are the active chat's, read through activeConversationId and
stored nowhere else. A new chat, and the replacement made when the active
chat is deleted, starts with a copy of the active chat's intent and no plan.
Resuming a chat makes it active and restores its model version; its intent
and plan never left it. A chat checkpoint keeps only the model version, the
boundary, the time and the card summary; the saved card reads its title and
headline from its own chat.

Region annotations belong with the model. Saved model versions held no
project-document state at all (restore always kept the current document, so
the old header comment about taking the earlier version's intent and plan was
wrong). Each version manifest now records the document's region list when it
is saved, a change to that list counts as a new version, and restoring or
resuming a version puts its list back.

The project-state schema is reset to version 1 with no migration, because
the project is not live yet: a document of any other version loads as a
fresh one, like a corrupt one. The older-record reads go with it (activity
source guessed from the correlation id, numbered default titles, the
skeleton merge and viewed-chat backfill), as do the version store's
first-format HEAD, the version-1 current-state wrapper and per-version
state.json reads. Project-state files saved during development load as fresh
documents and lose their chats.

The setup card shows the plan's headline in place of the preset-difference
rows, in every card state, and no line when there is no plan. The
"N objects with overrides" note stays on its own line. plan_set pushes the
card's context when it succeeds. The detailed setup page keeps every
difference, in OrcaSlicer's own preset/page/group order. Removed: the card's
difference selection, ranking, "more changes" count and "No changes from
presets" line, and the agent-authorship layer (remembering patch results,
replaying activities, binding to presets, the two maps).

Two intentional changes to the model's input, both in the re-recorded
tests/project_prompt/requests.json:
- preset differences no longer carry "origin";
- the in-app agent's own edits no longer mark its plan needs_reassessment.
  A person's edit (Undo and Redo included), an external MCP client's edit
  and a version restore still do. The recording's 240 needs_reassessment
  values are now current.
A third: a new chat's model sees no plan until it calls plan_set; before,
it inherited the previous chat's. plan_set's description now asks for a
short strategy headline (about 8 to 12 words) and a refresh when the
strategy changes.

Entire-Checkpoint: 01M5BEAGNDKC4S0C90G4QA26CE

2026-10-20T04:14:23.692Z | Mostly yes, I think it's how we prompted it, and it isn't new with the merged tool. That's a hypothesis from the transcripts, not something I've tested.

**The evidence: the old tool did the same.** Batch B still used `intent_update`, whose description said only "Record the user's explicit purpose as setupTitle". Seven of its twelve titles already carried settings or strategy:

- "PETG wall hook for 5 kg backpack - 6 walls, 25% infill"
- "Wall hook for 5 kg backpack - PETG HF, Strength profile, Textured PEI Plate"
- "Rhino figurine — 0.16mm, 3 walls, organic supports"
- "Display vase for dried flowers — Spiral Vase mode, PLA, X1C"

So the merge didn't cause this. It made it more visible, because title and headline now come from the same call and you can see them repeat each other.

**Why I think the prompting invites it:**

1. **The field's name says "setup", not "purpose".** It's called `setupTitle`, so a model reads it as "a title for the setup" and describes the setup. Field names tend to weigh more than the sentence explaining them.
2. **The title gets no limits; the headline gets several.** For the headline I wrote what to leave out (the purpose, the file name, the printer, routine steps) and a word target. For the title there's nothing like "no settings, material or printer". In practice the only rule it has is the 120-character limit.
3. **The model doesn't know what else the card shows.** Nothing tells it the presets line and the headline sit right under the title. So it packs everything into the title to make it stand on its own.
4. **The surrounding wording points the same way.** The project prompt says "a setup that suits the print's purpose, recorded with setup_record", which reads as "record the setup". And the `fields` show the same habit: the model filled them with "Printer=Bambu Lab X1 Carbon" and "Material=PLA", copying configuration rather than what the person said.

A cheaper, less capable model like DeepSeek V4 Flash probably follows names over prose more than a stronger one would. But all four points are in our wording, so that's where I'd fix it first.

**What I'd change:**
- Rename `setupTitle` to `purpose`.
- Describe it as the person's goal in a few words, in their terms, with no settings, material or printer unless the person made those the goal. Add one good and one bad example.
- Lower its limit to about 60 characters.
- Say in one line that the card shows the presets and the headline under it.
- Reword the project prompt line to "the print's purpose, recorded with setup_record". It's a small code change plus a re-recording, with no live calls.

To check the fix, the cheapest test is the standard project-prompt evaluation. Its `prepare-petg-strong` case grades exactly this first call, so I'd add a check that the title contains no settings. Any live run still needs Kenneth's approval of a specific batch.

Do you want me to make the change on this branch?

It loads one model into a clean project with the live Agent, writes `turn-N.json` (conversation, every tool call with arguments and result, pictures as `.b64`) once the chat has been quiet for 8 s, then waits for `next-N.txt` holding the next user message or `END`. The run script and viewer were `run_probe.sh` and `show_turn.py` in that session's scratchpad; the key comes from `JusPrin2.conf` through `OPENAI_API_KEY`, with a scratch `$HOME` per run.

Measured cost on gpt-5.4-mini: 3 conversations (file-load message plus 2 user turns each) were 31 requests and 267,803 tokens, 82% of the input cached. Real tool results, no canned replies, so it fits [[prompt-eval-spend-budget]].

Thingiverse: `curl` on `https://www.thingiverse.com/download:<id>` gets a 403 bot check. Open `thing:<id>/files` in the built-in browser, `find` the "Download <name>" button and click it; the file lands in `~/Downloads`.

Result of that session's test (current core prompt, 55a2d37618): in 3 of 3 conversations the assistant never called `view_render`, never said what the model was, and sliced with stock settings; see [[project-prompt-eval-sample-size]] for why 3 runs is an observation, not a rate.

Some product state is not held anywhere in OrcaSlicer: the print intent, the pinned agent plan, semantic region annotations, physical facts the user confirmed about a printer, and the monitoring rules the user sets for automatic pausing. For this state, the "current Orca owner" step in the route above is a JusPrin store instead. Every other step stays the same. The rules are:

State that belongs to a printer (confirmed facts, monitoring policy) stays in app data, stored per printer identity, the way `PrinterFactsStore` keeps it. Confirmed facts carry an expiry, because the physical world changes without telling the app. See [Local autosave and version history](autosave-version-history.md).

- **Revision.** Every write has to signal that it happened, so that readers read again. Two questions are still **open**: which signal to use, and whether the signal invalidates actions that are already queued. They belong to the milestone that adds the first writer. The obvious answer would be to publish a `WorkspaceChangeReasons` bit and add that bit to `kInvalidatingReasons`. That cannot be built as described. `settings_apply_patch` requires its caller's `expectedRevision` to equal the current revision exactly. So if the revision goes up at any point between a client's preview and its apply, the apply fails as `stale_workspace`. An agent that recorded its plan between previewing and applying would make its own call fail. There is an existing example of the alternative: the edit feed (`WorkspaceEditHub`) reports a change without raising the revision. Decide separately for each kind of state. A region annotation generates OrcaSlicer artifacts, so it is a real change to the project. An answer about intent, or a statement of the plan, is not. In the code as built, writing a region record signals nothing by itself. The artifacts it generates are ordinary OrcaSlicer edits, and they raise the revision in the usual way. So an action that was queued before an annotation goes stale, exactly as it would after any other edit to the model.
